item.title: Optimization of Urban Shortest Path Considering Traffic Congestion and Air Quality Using ICAW and Genetic Algorithm (Case Study: Tehran)
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — This study proposes a multi-objective framework for optimizing urban shortest paths by simultaneously considering traffic congestion and air quality. The objective is to minimize a weighted combination of travel time and pollutant exposure, with binary decision variables representing route selection. Real-world air quality data (SO₂, NO₂, CO) were collected from IoT sensors on 500 vehicles and 50 fixed stations across Tehran, integrated with traffic data via spatio-temporal synchronization using inverse distance weighting and 500m grid mapping. item.title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a disaster-aware privacy-preserving federated learning (PP-FL) solution for multi-city traffic flow prediction in heterogeneous and non-IID data settings. item.description: Computers, materials & continua/Computers, materials & continua (Print) — Fire threatens human life, property, and ecosystems, and recent years have seen frequent fire incidents worldwide. Video surveillance combined with deep learning has become a common strategy for fire and smoke detection. However, existing detectors often lose accuracy and robustness when targets are small, amorphous, or blurred against complex outdoor backgrounds. item.title: Measuring Activity-Space Segregation with Multi-Source Big Data: A Physical--Digital Framework with Simulation Validation and a Real-Data Proof of Concept
item.description: PhilPapers (PhilPapers Foundation) — Segregation research increasingly measures who people encounter beyond home, yet physical mobility, place semantics, and digital activity are often combined without clear construct boundaries. This study develops a physical--digital activity-space framework that distinguishes co-presence, digital exposure, and digital interaction, and represents physical and digital segregation as separate components rather than a forced composite. item.title: SUSTAINABLE MOBILITY AND TERRITORIAL ACCESSIBILITY IN MANIZALES, COLOMBIA: SOCIAL COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS OF AN EXPANDED AERIAL CABLE NETWORK
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — This research evaluates the socioeconomic feasibility of expanding the aerial cable car system in Manizales and Villamaría, Colombia, through a Social Cost-Benefit Analysis (SCBA). The assessment compares the three operational lines with a projected nine-line network, based on the Manizales Land Use Plan. The objective is to quantify and monetize impacts on CO2eq emissions, territorial accessibility, road safety, and public health benefits derived from induced active mobility. item.title: The Geography of Euroleague Basketball: Spatial Inequality, Travel Exposure and Home-Court Advantage in a Transnational League
item.description: Geosport for Society — This study conceptualizes the EuroLeague as a transnational urban network and tests whether spatial position and nominal travel distance are associated with competitive outcomes. The design integrates three empirical layers: (i) a longitudinal spatial panel covering the league-format era from 2016-17 to 2025-26; (ii) a completed 2025- 26 cross-section of 20 clubs in 17 nominal urban nodes and 11 countries; and (iii) a game-level model based on 1,943 available regular-season games from seven analytically retained seasons between 2016-17 and 2024-25. item.description: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems — Disaster image classification emerged as an important research area for supporting rapid disaster assessment, situational awareness, and emergency response operations.Nevertheless, accurately distinguishing among different disaster categories remains challenging due to large intra-class variations, complex backgrounds, and the limited capability of existing approaches to simultaneously capture local visual patterns, global contextual dependencies, and inter-feature relationships.To tackle these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Transformer-Graph Neural

item.title: STRATEGIC SPATIAL PLANNING FOR ENHANCING THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF THE TOURISM SECTOR IN GOA, INDIA
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. The analysis uses a 1 × 1 km grid across Goa and integrates tourism amenity indicators, environmental conditions, accessibility measures, and regulatory constraints. item.title: DELINEATION OF AGRICULTURAL FIELD BOUNDARIES USING MACHINE LEARNING: BASED ON THE CASE OF THE ZHETYSAI DISTRICT, KAZAKHSTAN
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is essential for agro-production monitoring, irrigation management, and sustainable land use planning. Manual digitization is labour-intensive and poorly scalable, while conventional segmentation algorithms are sensitive to spectral heterogeneity and weak inter-field contrast. The Zhetysai district of southern Kazakhstan – where approximately 45-50% of irrigated farmland exhibits salinization – exemplifies the urgent demand for automated field mapping. item.title: MORE MONUMENTS, MORE TOURISTS? EXAMINING HERITAGE-TOURISM RELATIONSHIPS ACROSS ROMANIAN COUNTIES
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Cultural heritage is an important territorial resource for tourism development, yet the relationship between the distribution of listed heritage assets and tourism activity remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the geographical relationships between listed cultural heritage and tourism in Romania, focusing on territorial disparities and long-term changes. item.title: Rethinking Women’s Football Attendance in an Emerging Destination: Constraints, Marketing Awareness and Interest through a Pluriversal Lens
item.description: Geosport for Society — Women’s football is increasingly recognised as an important component of the sport tourism industry, with potential to diversify audiences, stimulate domestic travel, and advance gender inclusivity in emerging destinations. Yet, despite the growing interest, attendance remains inconsistent, complicating conventional measures of spectator demand. item.description: Revista de Aplicaciones de la Ingeniería — In this article we highlight the importance of monitoring polluting particles in cities. This is to contribute to achieving sustainability objectives. Air pollution by suspended particles, especially PM2.5 and PM10, is a serious public health problem in urban areas of Mexico, with measurable impacts on respiratory and cardiovascular mortality and morbidity. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Illegal trade in lobster pueruli (Benih Bening Lobster, BBL) presents interconnected challenges for fisheries governance, coastal livelihoods, and Indonesia’s maritime defense. This study examines how changes in BBL utilization policies, legal market access, and commodity traceability create potential vulnerabilities that may be exploited by smuggling networks. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Indonesia’s customs administration operates at the intersection of maritime mobility, trade facilitation, border protection, and revenue assurance, yet its risk systems are still primarily organized around declarations, manifests, entities, and transactions rather than the wider maritime operating picture. This article develops a conceptual model for transforming Maritime Domain Awareness into a Customs Risk Picture that can support earlier, more contextual, and more explainable targeting of vessels, voyages, cargoes, and commercial actors. item.title: Between emergency and reconstruction: Territorial impacts and climate adaptation challenges after hurricane John in Guerrero
item.description: ECORFAN eBooks — This chapter analyses the territorial, human, and socioeconomic impacts caused by Hurricane John (2024) in the state of Guerrero, with a particular focus on the municipalities of Acapulco and Coyuca de Benítez, within a context of increasing intensity and frequency of extreme hydrometeorological events. item.title: PROTECTION OF FAMILIES AFFECTED BY THE MOUNT SEMERU ERUPTION: A DISASTER FIQH PERSPECTIVE ON THE MDMC LUMAJANG RESPONSE
item.description: Jurnal Al-Ijtimaiyyah — The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru not only destroyed homes but also severed the social and economic networks of thousands of families in Lumajang Regency, demanding a disaster response grounded in Islamic normative principles alongside technical capacity. Muhammadiyah, through the Himpunan Putusan Tarjih (HPT), has formulated Disaster Fiqh as an ethical framework to safeguard the rights of disaster victims, yet studies examining how far humanitarian organizations’ field practices align with this framework at the family level remain scarce. item.description: Problems of Social Hygiene Public Health and History of Medicine — The accessibility of social environment for people with disabilities is major condition of social rehabilitation and increasing their individual social mobility based on equal possibilities. By means of social mobility, people with disability receive access to various public benefits and possibility to lead comprehensively rich life. However, in Russian regions barriers of social environment remain to be significant. item.title: How Does Early Random Exploration Shape Content Allocation on Platforms? Evidence from a Large-scale Field Experiment
item.description: AIS Electronic Library (AISeL) — Digital content platforms must recommend new content before knowing its quality or audience fit, while early feedback is selectively shaped by prior allocation rules. Although exploration may support learning, direct evidence is limited regarding whether early random exploration improves the subsequent organic recommendation performance of new content by generating more informative feedback. item.title: Contribution of agricultural cooperatives and humanitarian assistance on food security resilience and rural development in Mali
item.description: ORBi (University of Liège) — Mali, located in the Sahel region, experiences a persistent food security crisis driven by climate variability, recurrent conflict, displacement, market disruptions, and structural weaknesses in rural systems. The agricultural sector, which supports the majority of households, is highly vulnerable to droughts, erratic rainfall, flooding, and insecurity. item.title: AI-Enabled Internet Of Things For Smart Cities: Applications, Challenges, And Future Research Directions - A Review
item.description: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology — The rapid growth of urban populations has increased the demand for efficient, sustainable, and intelligent urban infrastructure. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT), commonly referred to as Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT), offers promising opportunities to address these challenges through real-time data collection, intelligent analysis, predictive modelling, and automated decision-making. item.title: Comparative Framework of Vulnerability in Coastal Communities of the Ecuadorian Tropics
item.description: Applied Planetary Health — This study conducts a comparative analysis of socio-ecological vulnerability in six coastal communities of the Ecuadorian tropics, integrating mixed methods (quantitative and qualitative). The conceptual framework based on the components of Exposure, Sensitivity, and Adaptive Capacity allowed the construction of a Comparative Coastal Vulnerability Index (CCVI). item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary intellectual and social movement that connects gender equality, environmental sustainability and social justice. It examines how systems of patriarchy, economic exploitation, unequal resource distribution and environmental degradation can reinforce one another. item.title: Urban Context and Travel Experience Events: An Exploratory Comparison of Two German Cities
item.description: AHFE international — The presented study investigates associations between events influencing public transportation experience in both urban (Hamburg) and rural (Tuttlingen) areas in Germany, with the aim of identifying events associated with travel experience, which may in turn influence travel behavior. Using a mobile application, 21 participants in Tuttlingen and 70 participants in Hamburg tracked everyday trips, providing real-time evaluations of travel experiences along with situational data. item.description: Journal of Ecological Engineering — Lateritic nickel mining can increase the transport of metal-bearing particles into river systems, where sediment–water partitioning governs metal mobility and ecological exposure. Although redox conditions and organic matter are recognized as factors associated with metal partitioning, their relative importance under tropical lateritic mining conditions remains poorly understood. item.description: BMC Public Health — Background Staying physically active is essential for healthy ageing. Exposure to high levels of air pollutants such as particulate matter (PM) is associated with less active, more sedentary lifestyles in older adults. Whether results extend to typical fluctuations in daily PM exposure is unclear. We examined associations of higher-than-usual personal exposure to PM (PM 2.5 and PM 10) with next-day movement behaviour in older adults, assessed using concurrently worn personal air quality monitors and accelerometers. item.description: Frontiers in Public Health — Introduction Older adults’ well-being and its association with the environment have remained a prominent research focus with the rapid growth of the older adult population worldwide and the expansion of urban spaces. However, existing studies exploring perceived environmental factors for improving well-being mostly overlook the intrinsic association between perceived built and social environments in fostering well-being, and insufficiently address the potential variations of influencing factors within urban spaces. item.description: International Journal of Population Studies — Climate-related human mobility has become an important field of inquiry, yet its treatment across migration, adaptation, and governance scholarship remains conceptually fragmented. This study maps the development, intellectual structure, and substantive orientation of Scopus-indexed research on climate-related human mobility in the 16 member states of the Southern African Development Community (SADC). item.description: Australian Journal of Environmental Education — Schools are not only places where environmental issues are taught, but material settings in which environmental conditions shape participation, movement, outdoor activity and learning. This study analysed heat and solar exposure across Australian schools to examine whether environmental burden is structured by geography, remoteness, school type, sector and socio-economic context. item.description: International Journal of Wildland Fire — Background Public acceptance is part of successful fuels treatment implementation, especially in wildland–urban interface (WUI) areas near public lands. item.description: Frontiers in Marine Science — Introduction Under the background of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14 (Life Below Water), multi-agent collaborative governance of marine eco-economic systems faces prominent practical challenges. Coastal social-ecological vulnerability assessment and dynamic prediction are essential to support scientific marine governance. item.description: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR) — Background: An open fire gives you heat exactly where you need it (a street vendor, a night watchman, someone sleeping outside, etc.). item.title: Energy storage regimes as a framework for interpreting energy transitions
item.description: Frontiers in Sustainable Resource Management — Energy transitions are commonly framed as shifts in primary energy supply, with energy storage treated as a technical adjunct rather than a structural feature of socio-technical systems. This paper develops the concept of energy storage regimes to examine the role of storage in the development of human societies and its implications for contemporary decarbonisation. item.title: Associations between grandmothers’ and mothers’ air pollution exposure and preterm birth among black and white families in South Carolina, United States
item.description: Air Quality Atmosphere & Health — Preterm birth rates are persistently higher among Non-Hispanic Black (Black) versus Non-Hispanic White (White) individuals in the United States. Intergenerational influences may play a role. We combined birth records across three generations in South Carolina (1989–2020) and linked them with annual air pollution estimates from the census tract of maternal residence. item.title: Everyday encounters on the bus: courtesy and incivility in public transport
item.description: European Transport Research Review — Understanding everyday social interactions in public transport is key to creating more inclusive and pleasant travel experiences. We investigate the nature of social interactions on buses by observing and recording the behaviours of passengers and drivers throughout a bus journey in Stockholm, the capital of Sweden. item.title: From revolutionaries to citizens: assessing gender norm change in post-conflict Nepal
item.description: Frontiers in Political Science — Introduction This paper argues that Nepal’s conflict and protest history has been associated with real change in gender norms, but this change is uneven across the levels at which norms operate and across the social groups navigating them. This paper distinguishes gender norm change at the individual level of personal attitude and identity, the interactional level of what people expect of one another in daily encounters, and the institutional level of law, party structure, and government. item.title: Stormwater Runoff from the University of Southern California, University Park Campus: Potential Hazards and Drivers of Dissolved and Particulate Pollution
item.description: EarthArXiv (California Digital Library) — Climate models predict that Southern California will begin experiencing longer periods of drought and more intense storms in the coming decades. Long periods of drought have the potential to allow for the buildup of pollutants on undisturbed areas, such as the roofs of buildings and in gutters. item.description: Research Square — Walking-supportive neighborhoods are important for population health, yet macroscale walkability indices can obscure street-level conditions and their equitable distribution. This cross-sectional study explored how neighborhood income and demographic composition relate to microscale pedestrian infrastructure and whether these income-related differences in microscale features are moderated by macroscale walkability. item.description: Research Square — (150 words) Urban overheating threatens efforts to expand low-carbon active mobility, yet cities lack scalable methods to identify where heat most affects cyclists. item.description: East African Journal of Environment and Natural Resources — Flooding is a major natural hazard that continues to affect livelihoods and socioeconomic development in Bugarama Valley, Rusizi District, Rwanda. item.title: Characterizing fire monitoring actors and collaboration networks in Canada
item.description: International Journal of Digital Earth — Monitoring wildland fires using Earth observation data provides critical information on where and how fires are burning. Increasing pressures in fire management call for greater collaboration, inclusion, and user engagement.
